item.name: Ask the user for a mandate

request.name: Ask the user for a mandate

description.content:
The agent's operator asks its user for a mandate with these limits, as an RFC 8628 device authorization: the user opens `verification_uri_complete`, compares `user_code` and approves on Keelson's page with a passkey, lowering any limit. Only a client that linked an operator may ask, and the mandate names that operator. The code expires in 15 minutes and is single use.

An app acting for a user with a token they granted it (`mandates:request`) asks that user only: the request is theirs from the start, so it carries no number to match. The mandate names the app's own operator, or Keelson's hosted operator when the app has none. Through the hosted operator, every app is capped (`hosted-cap`): one user's open mandates and purchases of the last 180 days with apps whose redirect URIs are not a known host's may not pass `HOSTED_CAP_PER_USER_MINOR`, and with all such apps `HOSTED_CAP_KNOWN_PER_USER_MINOR`; every user's funded exposure may not pass `HOSTED_CAP_TOTAL_MINOR`.

description.content: A dry run: what a countersign of this cart would find, field by field, from the same policy set the TEE legs run, with nothing signed, reserved or logged. The countersign stays the only decision. An app acting for a user (`purchases:write`) checks only under a mandate that user approved for it.

description.content: Sends the cart to the TEE legs in order and returns the countersignatures only when both agree. A DENY is countersigned too. An app acting for a user (`purchases:write`) countersigns only under a mandate that user approved for it; under a mandate of Keelson's hosted operator it sends `mandateId` and Keelson closes the mandate with that operator's key over the request id and this cart, and nothing else. A cart is bought once per mandate: while a purchase of the same cart is in flight, or for ten minutes after it was captured, another request for it is answered `409 purchase-exists` with that purchase's id, whatever its request id, evidence or `Idempotency-Key`. Retrying after a lost answer is therefore safe; to buy the same cart again on purpose, name that purchase in `repeatOf`.

info.name: Keelson API (PayPal sandbox)
info.description: The operations an app or an operator's agent calls on Keelson: ask for a mandate, seal evidence, countersign a cart, and read and verify the Alibi. Sign in with Get New Access Token (OAuth 2.0 with PKCE). Payments run on the PayPal sandbox; no real money moves.
